description: Authored rationale for the flop c-bet decision (HU single-raised pot, hero = preflop aggressor in position vs BB). Keyed by opener/caller pairing; texture/hand-category scoring itself is unchanged (backend/app/domain/postflop.py::grade_cbet). Source: docs/research/02-postflop-strategy.md §2-3, 06-postflop-reference-tables.md.

rationale_parts.lead: As the button raiser you keep both edges into this flop — the stronger range AND position — so c-betting (continuing to bet as the raiser) is your default.
points: On dry, high boards, bet small and often: the big blind's calling range mostly missed and struggles to continue.
On wet boards (lots of possible draws), size up — you still hold the stronger strong hands, and draws will pay more to chase.

rationale_parts.lead: From the cutoff your range edge over the big blind is a notch smaller than the button's, but the in-position c-bet is still the default play.
points: Keep the c-bet frequency high on dry, high boards — your tighter range still hits them harder than the big blind's calls.
Slow down on low, connected, wet boards: that's where the big blind's wide calling range catches up.

rationale_parts.lead: Your UTG range is the strongest and narrowest of the raising seats, so track the board texture harder than any other seat would.
points: High, dry boards are yours — they're full of the big pairs and Broadways you raised with — so bet them confidently.
Low, connected boards favor the big blind's much wider calling range: cut the c-bet frequency fastest there.
